newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-HOLDERS AUXERRE NEED PENALTIES TO WIN CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HOLDERS AUXERRE NEED PENALTIES TO WIN CUP TIE.

text.p: Holders Auxerre needed a penalty shoot-out to move past Lens in a French Cup second round match on Saturday.

Extra time ended with the scoresheet still blank after a tense but dull match. A brilliant save by Auxerre keeper Lionel Charbonnier from a shot by Michael Debeve proved decisive, earning the club from Burgundy a 5-4 win in the shoot-out.
"It was a tough match which could have gone either way," said Auxerre's international defender Sabri Lamouchi. "But Lens are a good team and we knew what to expect."

The match was one of three clashes between first division clubs. Nice, bottom of the league, scored an uspet by knocking out third-placed Bastia on penalties on Friday and on Saturday Lille beat Lyon 1-0 thanks to a Djezon Boutoille goal in the 69th minute.

Rennes were the only first division side to bow out to a club from a lower division. The team from Brittany, still unbeaten at home in the league this season, fell 1-0 before their home fans to second division Troyes with Stephane Laquait scoring the winner for the visitors in the 59th minute.

Paris St Germain were made to work hard by third division Fecamp and it was not until the 75th minute that Cyrille Pouget headed them into the lead. Another goal by Julio Cesar Dely Valdes seven minutes later saw the Paris club win 2-0.
